title: Gridline: fine-tuning and batch inference on open models, OpenAI-compatible
excerpt: Gridline is the API for training your own AI models and running them in batch: fine-tuning, distillation and batch inference. Text fine-tuning and batch are live today: sign up and get free credit to start.
content_html:
Use arrow keys to choose a tile. Press Enter or Space to flip it and its neighbours.

Make a model thatspeaks in your voice

One API for fine-tuning, distillation and batch inference.

Backed by

What you can build

Teach a model your work, then run it on all of it

Start from a working recipe

Classify and route

Tickets, intents, documents, risk flags, on your labels.

Extract structured data

Pull fields from contracts, invoices and logs.

Embed a whole corpus

Embed millions of passages in one batch.

Distil a large model into a small one

Label with a large model, train a small one.

Transcribe speech

Tune speech recognition to your vocabulary.

Understand images and video

Caption and tag image and video libraries.

Why Gridline

The model is yours. The infrastructure is ours.

  • You own what you train

    Download the weights. No lock-in.

  • Pay for work, not waiting

    No endpoint to keep warm, no idle GPU.

  • Nothing new to learn

    Already on OpenAI's API? Two lines to switch.

Fine-tuning

Turn your examples into a model that does the job

  • Upload your examples and start training with one call. No GPUs to choose, no cluster to look after.
  • See how much better it got: every job scores the model before and after training.
  • Every fine-tune is quoted before it runs, paid from your credits, and ends with a model that is yours to keep.
Start fine-tuning
Batch inference

Run a model over everything you have

  • Hand over one file of requests and collect one file of results. No queue to build, no servers to scale.
  • Use a catalog model, or the model you just fine-tuned, in the same call.
  • Built for the big offline jobs: labelling datasets, clearing document backlogs, embedding entire corpora.
Start a batch
Distillation

Turn a large model into a small, fast, cheap one

  • A large open model answers your prompts in one batch, and a small model trains on its answers. It takes a few API calls.
  • Bring prompts and training data you own, and keep the small model you train: download it, or run your batches on it here.
  • You pay for the batches and the fine-tune it runs, from your credits. There is no separate distillation fee.
Start distilling

Same client

Keep the client you already use

Point OpenAI's Python client at Gridline and your first fine-tune is three calls away.

quickstart.py

import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://api.gridlinegpu.com/openai/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["GRIDLINE_TOKEN"],
)

training = client.files.create(file=open("train.jsonl", "rb"), purpose="fine-tune")
job = client.fine_tuning.jobs.create(model="qwen3.5-9b", training_file=training.id)
print(job.gridline["quote"])  # an estimate, before the job runs
Full quickstart

We believe intelligence should be cheap enough to be everywhere, and owned by the people who use it.

For agents

Hand the docs to your agent

Most code that calls Gridline will be written by an agent. So every page here can be read without a browser, and the API is the one your agent already knows.

  • One index

  • Every page as Markdown

  • An API it already knows

Paste this into your agent

Help me use Gridline (https://gridlinegpu.com): managed fine-tuning and batch inference on open models, through an OpenAI-compatible API.

Before you write any code, read https://gridlinegpu.com/llms.txt and the docs it links. Every page there is also plain Markdown: add .md to its URL.

Rules:
- Base URL: https://api.gridlinegpu.com/openai/v1. My token is in the GRIDLINE_TOKEN environment variable. Never print it, paste it or commit it.
- Use the OpenAI client I already have. Do not add another SDK.
- Fine-tunes are quoted before they run, and every job is paid from my prepaid credits. Show me the quote, or the cost you expect, and wait for my yes before you create a fine-tune or a batch.
- Use only the models and parameters the docs list. If the docs do not cover something, say so instead of guessing.
